entry.title: Learning and Certification for the AI Era: SAP Completes the Transformation of Certification
entry.content:
The Speed of Change Has Changed

In the age of AI, many would argue that we're experiencing something different from previous technology shifts: a collapse of time. New technologies, business models, and ways of working are emerging faster than organizations can absorb them.

According to LinkedIn's Talent Velocity research, 86% of organizations say they cannot upskill their workforce fast enough to keep pace with business demands.

As work changes, learning and certification must evolve as well. Professionals need more than theoretical knowledge, they need the ability to solve real-world challenges, work effectively with AI-powered tools, and continuously adapt as technology evolves.

Certification for the AI Era

The transformation of SAP Certification reflects this new reality.

Following the rollout announced earlier this year, the full SAP Certification portfolio now features practical, hands-on assessments designed to validate real-world skills rather than the ability to recall information. Learners can now choose from more than 100 certifications that assess their ability to solve business challenges, complete tasks in SAP systems, and apply their knowledge in realistic scenarios.

Just as AI is becoming part of everyday work, it is also becoming part of the certification experience. Through the open-book assessment approach, learners are encouraged to use available resources during their time-boxed exams, reflecting the realities of customer projects where professionals must work efficiently, solve problems under pressure, and leverage the tools available to them. This includes SAP Joule for Consultants, which is now available within selected certification exams to support learners in much the same way it supports consultants in their day-to-day work (phased rollout to follow).

More than 100,000 certification exams have already been taken under this new model, making SAP one of the first major enterprise software vendors to implement AI-enabled, performance-based certification assessments at scale.

As the transition to the practical exam portfolio has now been completed, the focus has shifted toward stabilization and continuous improvement. Learner feedback collected through post-exam surveys, support interactions, discussions here on SAP Community, and other channels directly influence roadmap priorities and enhancement planning.

Several improvements are already underway, including expanded language support and enhanced score reporting capabilities. Future score reports will provide greater transparency into performance across individual topic areas, helping learners better understand their results. If a learner does not pass an exam, these insights will make it easier to identify knowledge gaps and focus preparation efforts for the next attempt.

At the same time, SAP continues to invest in platform stability, user experience improvements, and support processes. The goal remains unchanged: creating a certification experience that is practical, transparent, reliable, and aligned with the realities of modern SAP work.

Learning the AI Way with SAP Learning Hub

Certification is just one side of the coin. SAP is also reimagining the learning experience.

To help SAP professionals upskill faster and in their preferred format, SAP Learning Hub now incorporates AI-assisted capabilities that make learning more personalized, interactive, and aligned with the way professionals learn today.

Learners can ask questions and receive answers grounded in SAP learning content in more than 80 languages. AI-generated study guides, quizzes, FAQs, podcasts, interactive AI-hosted learning experiences, and mind maps help learners engage with content in the formats that work best for them.

More than 13,000 early users have already embraced these capabilities to personalize their learning experience and accelerate skill development. Organizations are seeing measurable impact as well. LTIMindtree has reported significantly faster onboarding, while NTT DATA Business Solutions uses SAP Learning Hub as a key component of preparing talent for an increasingly AI-driven future.

The result is a more adaptive learning experience; one that helps learners spend less time navigating content and more time building practical skills.

A Milestone Year for SAP Skills

As SAP Certification approaches its 30th anniversary in 2026, the program is entering a new chapter.

Over the past three decades, SAP Certification has helped millions of learners validate their expertise and advance their careers. Today, the focus is evolving from knowledge validation alone to practical skill validation, helping ensure that learning, certification, and real-world job performance are more closely aligned than ever before.

Looking Ahead

The pace of change isn't slowing down, and neither is the evolution of SAP Learning and SAP Certification.

As AI becomes increasingly embedded in the way professionals learn, work, and solve business challenges, SAP will continue investing in experiences that help learners build practical, future-ready skills.

Join the Conversation

As we celebrate 30 years of SAP Certification, we're excited about what's next. Learning, certification, and work are becoming more connected than ever, and AI is helping make that possible. We look forward to continuing this journey together and hearing your feedback as we shape the future of SAP skills.

entry.title: Start Your SAP Career on Coursera: Two Certificates to Get You There
entry.content:
Looking to start a career in SAP but not sure where to begin? You’re not alone and there’s now a clear, accessible path. Nearly 200 million learners are already using Coursera to start or change their careers, and SAP is part of that journey. 

Coursera offers two SAP Professional Certificates, designed for accessibility and real career momentum. Self-paced, available in over 25 languages, needing no prior SAP experience, and completable in as little as 12 weeks. 

They are built for early-career professionals, students, and anyone looking to transition into SAP-related roles, offering a structured way to build confidence before stepping into the ecosystem.   

Each Coursera certificate targets a distinct role in the SAP ecosystem: 

  • SAP Technology Consultant Professional Certificate: Builds the core consulting skills SAP customers and partners look for, from requirements gathering and stakeholder management to solution design and navigating full SAP implementation lifecycles using SAP Activate. 
  • SAP Business Analyst Professional Certificate: Focuses on business analysis fundamentals, process modelling with SAP Signavio, data analysis with SAP Analytics Cloud, and how to bridge the gap between business requirements and technical delivery. 

Both are available on Coursera and carry ACE® (American Council on Education) credit recommendations. This means learners may be able to apply their learning toward academic credit at participating U.S. and Latin American universities. 

 The pathway to SAP Certification 

 These certificates don’t stop at foundational knowledge; they open the door to what comes next.  From there, learners can deepen their skills on SAP Learning site through self-paced courses and expert-led learning journeys. 

Ready to take the first step? Whether you’re starting your own SAP journey or supporting the next generation of talent, these certificates offer a practical and proven entry point into the ecosystem.

entry.title: Two Decades of Proven Excellence: Syntax Achieves SAP Golden Certificate While Driving Innovation
entry.content:
How do you keep mission-critical SAP environments running flawlessly while continuously pushing innovation forward? In this interview, Syntax shares how its deep SAP heritage shapes a modern, global approach to operations – and marks a major milestone along the way. By achieving SAP certification for the 10th consecutive time, Syntax has earned the prestigious Golden Certificate, underlining its long-standing commitment to quality and operational excellence. Combined with newly achieved global certifications in SAP Security Operations and SAP Business AI Operations, this recognition highlights Syntax's ability to deliver secure, future-ready services at scale. From cloud transformation to the growing role of SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) and AI, discover how Syntax helps customers turn SAP operations into a true driver of business value.

Could you start by telling us about your company and the services you offer?

Syntax is a global technology solutions and services provider with deep expertise in running and transforming mission-critical enterprise environments. We help customers manage complexity across cloud, applications, infrastructure, security, and end-user services, with SAP being one of our core strategic focus areas.

In the SAP space, we support customers across the full lifecycle: from advisory, migration, and implementation through to technical managed services, application management, optimization, and innovation. That includes operating highly business-critical SAP landscapes, supporting transformation to SAP S/4HANA and cloud-based environments, and helping customers unlock additional value through SAP BTP, automation, security, and AI.

What differentiates Syntax is our Boutique @ Scale approach. The ability to combine strong operational discipline with a forward-looking innovation mindset, tailoring every engagement to our customers' unique priorities. Customers come to us not only to keep their SAP environments stable and secure, but to evolve them as business needs change, backed by the agility and personal care of a boutique, delivered with the reach and resilience of a global enterprise.

 

 

Your SAP roots run deep, brought to Syntax through Freudenberg IT, whose SAP pedigree reaches back almost to SAP's founding. How has that heritage shaped who Syntax is today as an SAP operations partner – and is it still something you draw on?

Our heritage through Freudenberg IT has had a lasting impact on who we are as an SAP operations partner. It shaped a culture centered on reliability, accountability, process discipline, and long-term customer commitment, all of which remain essential when you are operating business-critical SAP environments.

That background gave us a very practical understanding of what enterprise customers need from an operations partner: not just technical expertise, but consistency, governance, responsiveness, and the ability to support transformation without compromising stability.

We absolutely still draw on that heritage today. While Syntax has evolved into a global organization with a broad portfolio and a modern cloud- and innovation-focused vision, the core DNA remains the same: trusted operations, deep SAP knowledge, and a commitment to helping customers run mission-critical systems with confidence.

 

Looking back at those early years of the partnership, what inspired your decision to seek your first service certification in 2002 – initially in Germany – and what then drove the decision to expand that certification globally in 2006?

From the beginning, we saw certification not simply as a badge, but as an important way to benchmark ourselves against SAP's own operational standards and to validate the quality of the services we were delivering to customers. Starting in Germany made sense because that was where our SAP operations heritage was strongest and where we had built deep experience in supporting complex customer landscapes. As customer expectations grew and our delivery model became increasingly international, expanding that certification globally was the next natural step. It reflected two priorities: first, giving customers the confidence that they would receive the same high-quality service wherever they operated; and second, creating a globally consistent operational framework across our teams. In that sense, certification supported both trust and scale.

Handover of the golden certificate, June 2026

 

How would you describe Syntax's SAP operations proposition to a customer who doesn't want to choose between operational reliability and continuous innovation?

Our message would be very simple: you should not have to choose between the two. At Syntax, we believe the strongest SAP operations model is one that protects the business today while enabling transformation for tomorrow. That means delivering stable, secure, and highly governed day-to-day operations while also helping customers adopt new capabilities in areas such as cloud, automation, SAP BTP, and AI.

We often describe this as helping customers optimize the "run" so they can invest more confidently in the "grow". In practice, that means reducing operational risk, increasing visibility, improving efficiency, and creating the right foundation for continuous innovation. For customers, the outcome is not just better uptime; it is a more agile SAP environment that supports long-term business change.

 

 

How do you experience the audits in practice, and what role do they play for your organization?

We see the audits as rigorous, constructive, and valuable. They are an important discipline for the organization because they require us to demonstrate - not just describe -  the maturity of our processes, controls, and service delivery practices.

In practice, audits help us maintain a strong level of operational consistency across teams and regions. They also create a useful feedback loop, highlighting where we are strong and where we can continue to improve. Internally, that reinforces accountability and continuous improvement; externally, it gives customers and SAP additional confidence in the quality and reliability of our services.

So for us, audits are not just compliance exercises. They are an important part of how we sustain operational excellence at scale.

 

For the first time, you achieved global certification for SAP security operations and SAP Business AI operations - can you tell us how your competencies around Security and Business AI operations are adding value to your service offerings?

These certifications are important because they reflect the evolving customer expectations. Today, customers want innovation, but they also want it delivered in a way that is secure, governed, and operationally robust. On the security side, our capabilities help customers strengthen the protection of their SAP landscapes through a combination of foundational controls, continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, privileged access governance, and broader security operations support. That adds value by reducing risk, improving visibility, and helping customers operate with greater confidence in increasingly complex hybrid environments.

On the Business AI side, the value is about helping customers move from interest to operational reality. It is one thing to explore AI use cases; it is another to run them reliably in enterprise environments. Our role is to help customers embed AI into their SAP landscape in a scalable, supportable way that is aligned with operational best practices. Together, Security and Business AI operations allow us to help customers innovate more safely and more effectively.

 

As SAP is strongly focusing on the cloud and encourages partners to support customers in their migration journey, how are you already helping customers in this area - and looking three to five years ahead, what role do SAP BTP and AI play in Syntax's vision and how do you expect your capabilities to evolve?

We are already supporting customers across the full cloud migration journey: from assessment and planning through migration, conversion, upgrade, and post-go-live operations. That includes helping customers modernize existing SAP environments, move to cloud-based operating models, and build the governance and support structures required for long-term success.

A major part of our value is that we do not view migration as a one-time project. We see it as part of a broader transformation of our operating model. Customers need a partner that can help them move, stabilize, optimize, and then continue to innovate.

Looking three to five years ahead, we see SAP BTP playing a central role as the platform for clean-core extensions, integration, automation, and data-driven innovation. We also expect AI to become much more deeply embedded - both in business processes and in the way SAP environments are operated and optimized. For Syntax, that means continuing to evolve our capabilities in platform operations, cloud governance, automation, observability, security, and AI-enabled service delivery. Our vision is to help customers build SAP operating models that are not only cloud-ready, but also innovation-ready.

 

If you could give one piece of advice to a customer who is just beginning to think about their SAP operations strategy for the next decade, what would it be?

If we had to highlight one key recommendation, it would be this: treat SAP operations as a strategic business capability rather than just a technical support function.

Over the next decade, organizations will need to balance resilience, security, cost efficiency, and continuous innovation far more closely than before. Those that succeed will be the ones who design their operating models early on, with standardization, automation, cloud readiness, and strong governance built in from the outset.

Ultimately, it is important not to separate your operations strategy from your transformation strategy. Reliable and well-governed operations are not just the foundation for stability - they are what make sustainable innovation possible.

 

Information on the certification program for operations partners, as well as an overview of all certified partners, can be found in the SAP Operations Partner Guide.

Visit OPC at SAP.com or on the SAP Partner Portal.

entry.title: Start a Career in SAP Consulting: A Structured Path on Coursera
entry.content:
The SAP Technology Consultant role sits at the heart of most implementations, translating business requirements into solutions and guiding projects from design through delivery. It’s also one of the most in-demand roles in the SAP ecosystem. 

For those looking to move into this space, the SAP Technology Consultant Professional Certificate on Coursera offers a clear and accessible starting point, no prior SAP experience needed. 

What the Coursera certificate covers 

The curriculum goes beyond product knowledge. Across seven courses, learners cover consulting skills, project management and tools like SAP S/4HANA A full hands-on implementation project puts it all into practice, producing real deliverables learners can mention in interviews. The final course focuses on career development and preparation for SAP Certification. 

Each course builds on the previous one. By the capstone, learners have worked through the full SAP implementation lifecycle twice: once with guidance, once independently. The certificate also carries ACE (American Council on Education) credit recommendations, meaning learners may be able to apply their learning toward academic credit at participating U.S. and Latin American universities. 

Who this is for 

The Coursera certificate is a strong starting point for anyone looking to enter SAP consulting. It's also useful for people already in the ecosystem who work alongside consultants and want a clearer picture of the full project lifecycle. 

From Coursera certificate to SAP Certification 

Completing the Coursera certificate is just the beginning. It builds foundational knowledge, with learners then deepening skills through SAP Learning site via self-paced courses and expert-led journeys. 

 Start learning on Coursera now: SAP Technology Consultant Professional Certificate

entry.title: Turn Business Needs into SAP Solutions: Start with This Business Analyst Path

The SAP Business Analyst role is one of the most valuable on any implementation project: bridging business stakeholders and technical teams, mapping processes, identifying gaps, and making sure that the solution fits the need. Demand for people who can do this well in an SAP context is consistently high. 

Looking to move into this space? The SAP Business Analyst Professional Certificate offers a structured starting point, no prior SAP experience required.

Who this is for

entry.title: 20 Years of Unbroken SAP Certification - How NTT DATA Turns Operations into a Strategic Edge
entry.content:
For more than 35 years, NTT DATA has been shaping how organizations run and transform their SAP landscapes – and their track record speaks for itself. The company has just received the Golden Certificate from SAP, marking their 10th consecutive certification and underscoring an unbroken commitment to quality that few partners can match. In an interview with Lars Janitz – Senior Executive, Head of Global Business & Managed Services at NTT DATA Business Solutions and Head of Global Practice SAP & ServiceNow at NTT DATA, Inc. – he reveals how NTT DATA helps customers balance rock-solid operations with continuous innovation, without compromising business continuity. From SAP BTP and AI to global security operations, he explains where the greatest opportunities lie in the years ahead. Read on to find out why Lars Janitz believes that a strong operational foundation today is the key to unlocking the full potential of cloud and AI tomorrow.

Could you start by telling us about NTT DATA and the services you provide to customers worldwide?

NTT DATA is a global leader in SAP consulting, implementation, managed services, and business transformation. For more than 35 years, we have been supporting organizations in implementing and modernizing their SAP landscapes, increasing the value of the SAP landscape, moving to modern cloud platforms, and driving business innovation.

What sets us apart is our ability to combine global scale, deep SAP expertise, and local customer proximity. We support customers throughout the entire SAP lifecycle – from strategy and implementation to operations, optimization, and continuous innovation.

Handover of the golden certificate, July 2026

Looking back at your long partnership with SAP, what motivated NTT DATA to pursue its first SAP operations certification in Germany in 2001, and what were the key factors behind expanding that approach globally in 2006?

Our original motivation was simple: to provide customers with independent proof of the quality and reliability of our SAP operations services. As our customers expanded internationally, they expected the same level of service and governance everywhere they operated. Extending the certification approach globally allowed us to create a consistent delivery model, support multinational customers more effectively, and establish the foundation for the global managed services organization we have today.

Many customers are seeking both stability and innovation in their SAP landscapes. How does NTT DATA help customers balance reliable operations with ongoing transformation and modernization?

We don't see stability and innovation as conflicting objectives. Reliable operations and deep industry knowledge create the foundation for successful transformation. Our teams ensure that customers' SAP environments run securely and efficiently while continuously identifying opportunities to improve and automate processes, adopt cloud technologies, and leverage new SAP functionalities. This allows customers to modernize at their own pace without compromising business continuity.

As SAP continues to accelerate cloud adoption, how is NTT DATA supporting customers on their transformation journey today, and where do you see technologies such as SAP BTP and AI creating the greatest opportunities over the next several years?

We help customers accelerate their cloud journey through a combination of advisory, implementation, managed services, and ongoing optimization. Our goal is to deliver business value, not just technical migration. Furthermore, we leverage our 360-degree partnership with SAP to enhance and innovate our services. 

Looking ahead, SAP BTP and AI will play a critical role in helping organizations integrate processes, extend applications, automate decisions, and unlock greater productivity. The biggest opportunity lies in turning trusted business data into actionable intelligence.

NTT DATA recently achieved global certification for SAP Business AI and SAP security operations. How do these capabilities complement your existing managed services portfolio, and what benefits are customers already seeing today?

These certifications are a natural next step in the evolution of our managed services portfolio. They strengthen our ability to operate SAP environments at scale, intelligently, and securely. For customers, this means faster adoption of AI technologies, stronger security governance, and greater confidence that innovation can be introduced without increasing operational risk.

How do you experience the audits in practice, and what value do they bring to your teams and customers?

We view audits as an opportunity to improve rather than simply a compliance requirement. They provide valuable external validation and help us continuously strengthen our processes, capabilities, and delivery standards. For customers, they provide assurance that our services are regularly assessed against rigorous SAP requirements and industry best practices.

Can you share an example of an insight or recommendation from a past audit that led to a meaningful improvement in the way you deliver services or engage with customers?

One recurring theme has been the importance of globally aligned service management combined with strong local execution. Those insights encouraged us to further standardize incident management, reporting, and governance across our delivery organization. As a result, customers benefit from greater transparency, more consistent service experiences, and improved responsiveness across regions.

With a broad portfolio of SAP operations certifications across multiple solutions and regions, what does this global consistency mean for customers in their day-to-day operations and transformation projects?

For customers, global consistency means trust and predictability. They know what level of service, governance, and expertise they can expect regardless of location. Whether they are running business-critical operations or executing a major transformation program, our standardized delivery approach helps reduce complexity, mitigate risk, and accelerate outcomes.

Looking ahead, how do you expect demand for SAP Business AI operations to evolve, and how is NTT DATA preparing its managed services organization to support that evolution globally?

We expect demand to increase rapidly as AI moves from experimentation to enterprise-wide adoption. Customers will increasingly need partners that can not only deploy AI but also operate and govern it effectively. We are investing in AI operations capabilities, delivery models, security, and talent development to help customers confidently and responsibly scale SAP Business AI across their organizations.

What advice would you give to organizations that are currently defining their SAP operations strategy for the years ahead?

Our advice is to view operations as a strategic enabler of innovation. A modern operations strategy should balance resilience, security, and efficiency with the ability to rapidly adopt new technologies and provide valuable outcomes. Organizations that build a strong operational foundation today will be much better positioned to take advantage of cloud, AI, and future SAP innovations tomorrow.

 

Information on the SAP certification program for operations partners, as well as an overview of all certified partners, can be found in the SAP Operations Partner Guide.

entry.title: Anuradha Dhingan's Framework: How an SAP Architect Turns Experience into Validated Expertise
entry.content:
For two decades, Anuradha Dhingan has built enterprise solutions across the SAP ecosystem. As a Development Architect at SAP Labs, she works across SAP S/4HANA, SAP BTP, and SAP Business AI, helping design the intelligent systems that support businesses around the world. But after twenty years in the industry, a different question began to matter: how do you make sure that years of experience continue to evolve alongside SAP itself? The answer wasn't to learn more, it was to validate everything years of experience had already taught her. 

That shift is reflected in the way she approaches learning today. She still jogs every morning through Gurugram to reset before the day begins. She still reads constantly, searching for what she calls "schematics", the frameworks and mental models that help her design better systems. But certification has become another part of that rhythm. "My approach with each certification is not to learn from the ground up," she explains. "It's to formalize real-world expertise." 

Rather than starting from scratch, Anuradha saw certification as a way to benchmark years of practical experience against SAP's latest standards. Each certification became an opportunity to validate what she knew, identify where the technology had evolved, and strengthen the foundations behind decisions she was making every day. The first certification confirmed her methods. The second sharpened her approach. By the fourth, she had integrated a powerful habit into her career. The learning paths and practical exercises on SAP Learning Hub provided a strategic narrative, bridging the gap between her high-level architectural designs and the tactical reality of implementation. 

She now holds SAP Certified credentials as a Solution Architect for SAP BTP, an Implementation Consultant for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, in Positioning SAP Business AI Solutions, and in SAP Business Data Cloud. Each one was a focused engagement that built upon her existing foundation. 

Anuradha presenting at an event.The impact became clear in her day-to-day work.  When she now leads architectural discussions with her team, she draws not only on years of practical experience but on knowledge that has been deliberately refreshed and validated. "Each certification cycle leaves me feeling re-energized and deeply empowered," she says. "I gain a profound confidence from knowing my skills are not just field-proven, but also officially validated and current." 

That confidence extends beyond projects. Whether mentoring colleagues, writing technical articles, speaking at SAP events, or contributing to the wider SAP community, she shares knowledge that has been continuously tested and kept current. For Anuradha, certification has become a professional ritual, as vital as the morning jog that clears her mind or the deep reading that provides her 'schematics'. Every so often, she deliberately tests her expertise, not as a simple proof of knowledge, but as an act of sharpening it. It is this unwavering commitment to self-validation that ensures she is always ready to build the future. 

Every certification starts as a small habit. Explore learning journeys and credentials on the SAP Learning site and see where yours leads.

entry.title: Learn how to get certified for BDC
entry.content:
Dear data engineers, dear business data jugglers, dear SAP Analytics Cloud and SAP BDC experts,

 

Why should you become a certified business data cloud (BDC) professional? 

Sure, to prove your knowledge and skills, increase your value as a consultant on the market, and therefore become involved in the most interesting and meaningful projects. After all, certified consultants are most recognized and well-paid.

 

What is the certification exam? 

SAP offers two types of exam: system based, and AI powered knowledge assessment. The exam for SAP BDC (C_BCBDC) is of the latter type. Simply talk to an AI avatar and prove your knowledge.

2 types of exam exist

 

Where do you find the certification exam? 

Go to our starting page, SAP Certified - SAP Business Data Cloud

SAP Certified - SAP Business Data Cloud

On that page, you find links to the training material and an option to book the exam.

 

How could you become a certified SAP BDC professional?

You may have heard about the AI based exam style which is new as of this year. But what is it all about?

In an online interview with an AI, you need to answer 20 - 30 questions around different BDC topics. do you need to wear a bow tie to pass? Go to the hairdresser first? Don't worry, the only thing that counts here is what you say. Give profound, full, and correct answers.

An interview with avatar Riley Bennet

 

How do we help you? 

To learn about our exam program and to prepare for it in the best way, we offer our "Get Certified" live sessions.

Learning objectives of our Get Certified live session

You may have many questions, for example what do you need technically to be interviewed, which language you should choose, which topics you need to explain, how the time-taking and pausing during the interview works,  and how you will be rated. And of course, you likely have your own specific questions.

In this case, you should join the  "Get SAP Certified - SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC)" live session on Aug 4th and 11th in which my colleagues and I give you some guidance and advice. We also will run these live session again on 9th and 16th November 2026.

Search here: Browse SAP Live Sessions

Find out about our offer and its dates and apply here: 

Get Certified: SAP Certified - SAP Business Data Cloud

Offered datas - Get Certifed SAP Business Data Cloud live sessions

The series consists of the following:

  • Kick-off session - Outlining the live session series, introducing the certification, explaining the certification format and exam interface, providing tips for preparation, explaining the learning journey self-study content, practice systems, and corresponding content review sessions - 1 hour
  • Content review session - Covering important certification-relevant topics from the courses that are part of the corresponding learning journey Exploring SAP Business Data Cloud.  This session does not teach the topics from scratch, but instead complements your self-study, providing you with the opportunity to get explanations and demonstrations from an expert, who can answer questions you have about the content, helping you to be better prepared for the certification - 1 hour

You can register for the kick-off and the content review session as a bundle.

 

Is this all?

Not quite. Don’t forget:

After passing the exam, your badge is valid for just one year. Within that year, you must take another exam which we call the “Stay certified”. Don’t worry – it’s easier. You just need to know some additional information and answer some additional questions, but you can retry answering them if you fail. To know what you will be asked about, watch the recording: Stay Certified - SAP Business Data Cloud.

See you soon – as a certified business data cloud expert🙂

Alexander

entry.title: An Ocean of Possibility: How Shivani Dwivedi Built Her SAP Career
entry.content:
The metro had three stops left when something clicked for Shivani Dwivedi. She was riding home with a colleague from the functional team at Aakash Educational Services Ltd., responsible for materials management having a conversation — not a formal discussion, just a conversation between stations. But she found herself asking questions she hadn't thought to ask before. How does material actually flow through a business? What is a purchase order, a service entry sheet?

As her colleague explained, piece by piece, something clicked. Not perfectly. Not all at once. But enough. For the first time, Shivani wasn't looking at isolated tasks. She was seeing a flow. A complete picture. Somewhere between those stops, a thought became clear. If I want to be a good developer, I first need to understand what I'm part of. 

She is an SAP ABAP Developer at Deloitte USI for more than a year now. 

Four years earlier, she had stepped out of college thinking she was prepared. She knew how to code. She understood logic. But SAP was different. "It felt like stepping into an ocean," she says. "Deep, structured, and endless." She was learning ABAP, the programming language behind much of SAP's business logic, but the requirements didn't make sense to her, not because they were wrong, but because she had no understanding of the ecosystem they belonged to. Everything felt connected. She just couldn't see the connections yet. 

The metro conversation changed how she learned. She stopped chasing answers and started staying with questions. And the way she answered those questions was through certification. 

When she wanted to be sure her foundations in the modern SAP development model were solid, she sat the SAP Certified Associate – Back-End Developer – ABAP Cloud exam. The certification didn't teach her ABAP, but it gave her a structured way to test what she knew against what the role required, surfacing corners of the language she'd never had to use before. 

That curiosity soon stretched beyond development. She started building dashboards for stakeholders almost as a side experiment, exploring how data could be presented in more meaningful ways. What began as curiosity quickly turned into something much bigger. As finance and technology leaders saw their financial and operational data through a new lens, more requests followed. Before long, she had become the go-to person for SAP Analytics Cloud within her team. 

By the time she completed the SAP Analytics Cloud certification, it wasn't simply another credential. It reflected a capability she was already using to solve real business problems, giving her greater confidence that the solutions she was building aligned with SAP's latest best practices. 

When low-code and no-code development started reshaping how applications got built, she earned the SAP Build Developer certification. And when generative AI began moving headlines into actual SAP workflows, she completed the SAP Generative AI Developer certification too. 

The Generative AI exam followed the new task-based format, which meant working through realistic scenarios rather than answering questions about them — fitting, given how Shivani had learned everything else: by breaking things in practice systems until they made sense. 

"The Generative AI certification felt like a milestone," she says, "but honestly, it was the icing. The real value was in the process: learning, experimenting, building." 

Four years in, what changed isn't really what she knows. It's how she learns. "Earlier, I thought learning meant finding answers. Now I think it means staying with questions." 

If you met Shivani on a Saturday morning now, you still probably wouldn't guess she works in tech. You'd find her in a quiet room with a cup of chai in one hand, a book in the other, surrounded by more books than she'll realistically finish. The Saturdays haven't changed. What has changed is the way she approaches learning, not by rushing towards answers, but by staying curious enough to keep asking better questions. 

Looking back, it's remarkable that one of those questions first took shape during an ordinary metro ride home. Four years later, she's still following it.

entry.title: Clearing SAP Backend Developer – ABAP Cloud Certification: My Take on the System-Based Assessment
entry.content:
I passed — 100% on the system-based assessment (cut score was 67%). But this post isn't a victory lap. It's just my perspective on what this exam actually feels like, because it caught me a little off guard, and I figured it might help someone else prepping for it.

Quick context first: SAP's certification methodology broadly has two flavors — system-based assessments and scenario-based assessments. These aren't two halves of the same certification; they're two different approaches SAP uses across different certs. This particular certification, the Back-End Developer, ABAP Cloud, is a system-based exam, so that's what this post is about. (I'll share my experience with a scenario-based certification separately, at another time — that was a different exam entirely.)

So What's It Actually Like?

You get dropped into a real SAP BTP ABAP Environment, open it in Eclipse with ABAP Development Tools (ADT), and you're handed some tasks - in my case it was 8. You don't pick an answer from a list — you actually build things, live, in the system.

Now, the specific objects you're asked to build will vary between candidates. So rather than walking through all eight in detail, here are just a few examples of the kind of thing you might be asked to do:

  • Set up your own package correctly, with the right super-package and transport request.
  • Build a class hierarchy with very specific rules about attribute visibility — public-readonly, protected, private — enforced strictly.
  • Generate a RAP Business Object from a table and wire up a field control and a determination.
  • Add a CDS access control on a copied CDS view using an authorization object.

That's just a taste — yours might look different. But the flavor is the same throughout: less "solve a puzzle," more "show me you know how to actually use these tools."

The Biggest Mental Shift: This Is Graded by Automation

This is the part that changes how you should approach the whole exam: your submission gets evaluated automatically, not by a human squinting and going "eh, close enough."

That means naming matters. Casing matters. If the instructions specify an exact object name, parameter name, or type, use exactly that — not your own convention, not something "basically the same." Read every naming and typing instruction twice before you touch the keyboard.

It's Not Really Testing Logic — It's Testing Familiarity

The biggest realization I had: this exam isn't mainly about clever algorithms. A task or two does test genuine logic-building, but even there, multiple valid solutions are acknowledged — the focus is on correct output, not elegance.

What it's really checking is whether you've actually worked hands-on with these object types before. Do you know how to set attribute visibility correctly without looking it up? Have you actually generated a RAP object before, not just read about RAP? That kind of muscle memory is exactly what separates someone who's built things in ADT from someone who's only studied the theory — and it's also why this format can't really be "dumped" the way old MCQ exams could.

🛠️ My Actual Tips & Tricks

1. Read every instruction line twice before touching the keyboard. Naming, exact types, exact visibility — all graded literally.

2. Watch the naming placeholder pattern closely. You'll get a group/seat number, and every object name has a placeholder you swap it into. Easy to slip up here — don't.

3. Let the syntax checker be your friend. You don't need to recall exact ABAP syntax from memory. Start typing — ADT will flag errors and warnings immediately. Read them, fix them, move on.

4. Don't just build — test what you built. I finished the required tasks in about 90 minutes of the 3 hours given. I used the rest of the time to write quick throwaway test code (IF_OO_ADT_CLASSRUN + MAIN), instantiate what I'd built, and actually run it — even stepping through with breakpoints where I wanted to be sure. None of that was part of the deliverable, but it caught small mistakes that would've otherwise slipped through.

5. Time is genuinely not the enemy. Three hours is generous. Don't rush your reading just because the clock is ticking.

6. Check your tool prerequisites before exam day. This exam needs a specific minimum version of Eclipse and ADT — don't assume an old install will cut it. Whatever system-based certification you're attempting, verify tool requirements days in advance, not the morning of.

7. Trust hands-on experience over memorized theory. If you've genuinely built classes, CDS views, RAP objects, and dictionary types in ADT before — even in small practice projects — you're most of the way there already.

The Bigger Picture

This format feels like a genuinely better test of whether someone can do the job, not just recall facts under pressure. If you've been meaning to get truly hands-on with ABAP Cloud development but have mostly stuck to reading docs — this exam is a good nudge to go build something first.

Good luck to everyone prepping for this — you've got this. 💪

entry.title: From One Exam to a Global Standard: The SAP Certification Story
entry.content:
Thirty years ago, SAP set out to answer a simple but important question: How do you prove that someone truly knows SAP? The answer became one of the most trusted credentialing programs in the industry. And this year, it turns 30. 

Three decades. Countless careers shaped. Every major technology shift in enterprise software, tracked and validated. SAP Certification did not just grow alongside the SAP ecosystem. In many ways, it helped build it. It gave customers confidence, gave partners credibility, and gave individual professionals something that no resume bullet point could replicate: proof. 

So, as we mark this anniversary, it is worth looking back at the moments that shaped it — and forward at what is still to come. 

1996: The Question That Started Everything 

 The question that opened this story became the foundation of SAP Certification. In 1996, the first computer-based certification exams launched in Germany, built on rigorous psychometric standards and covering core SAP R/3 modules. By the end of that first year, nearly 1,000 professionals had earned their credentials. A global standard had been born. 

The 2000s: A Career Framework Takes Shape 

As SAP's portfolio expanded, so did certification. New credentials followed by SAP NetWeaver, SAP Business One, and SAP SuccessFactors. Associate, Specialist, and Professional levels gave professionals not just a credential to earn, but a path to follow. Certification became a career framework, not just an exam. 

Going Global: Certification Without Borders 

 Certification began expanding beyond SAP locations between 2007 and 2011 through a partnership with Pearson VUE, bringing SAP Certification to test centers around the world. Remote proctoring later removed another major geographic barrier, allowing professionals to earn SAP Certification from wherever they were based. A consultant in Jakarta, Johannesburg, or Guadalajara could now sit the same exam to the same standard as someone in Walldorf or New York. Together, these milestones made SAP Certification truly global. 

2015: Ready for S/4HANA and the Cloud 

When SAP S/4HANA launched, it redefined what SAP expertise looked like. New credentials rose to meet it, giving professionals a way to prove they were ready for the transformation customers were counting on. The credentials and the platform evolved together, as they always had. 

 2014–2024: Learning, Badges, and Staying Current 

 The launch of SAP Learning Hub in 2014 brought learning and certification together into a single experience, providing a platform where professionals could learn, practice, and get SAP-certified. Digitalbadges offered via Credly, later made credentials visible and shareable across professional networks, while the Stay Current program transformed certification from a one-time achievement into a continuously validated credential. Today, SAP professionals demonstrate not only what they once learned, but that their skills remain up to date. 

 Certification Reimagined 

Since 2025, SAP Certification has entered its next chapter. Certification Reimagined is transforming how SAP expertise is validated by shifting the focus from knowledge recall to real-world skill validation. Instead of traditional multiple-choice exams, candidates complete practical, system- and scenario-based assessments that reflect real SAP roles and project work. They solve time-bound challenges in real-world SAP environments, with access to relevant resources and AI-supported tools, just as they would on the job.  This is not just a new exam format. It is a new definition of what certified means. 

 30 Years In, the Best Is Still Ahead 

This anniversary isn't only about celebrating the past. It's about preparing the workforce of the future. SAP has committed to equip 12 million people  with AI-ready skills by 2030, and certification is at the heart of that. As SAP Certification looks ahead, the focus remains on real skills, continuous learning, and an AI-first world. The standard that started with one exam in Germany is now shaping the future of work across the globe. 

Thirty years on, that original question still drives everything. And the answer has never been stronger.

entry.title: C_TS462_EN_2601: Understanding the New System-Based Exam Pattern
entry.content:
The SAP Certified – Implementation Consultant for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, Sales certification has taken a slightly different approach with the new C_TS462_EN_2601 exam pattern.

I recently went through this new format, and one thing that stood out to me was the shift from a mainly question-based assessment to a more practical, system-based assessment. This changes the way we should prepare for the certification as well.

This blog is based on my personal experience with the exam and my preparation journey. The exam structure and content may change over time, so candidates should always refer to the latest information provided by SAP.

What is different in the new exam pattern?
The biggest difference is that you are required to work with the SAP system and achieve a specific outcome.

In my experience, the assessment consisted of around 5 to 6 practical task groups. Each task provided a high-level requirement along with the expected outcome. The task does not necessarily take you through every step that needs to be performed.

This means you need to understand the requirement first, identify the relevant configuration or process, perform the required activities in the system, and finally make sure that the expected result is achieved.

The overall approach can be thought of as:

Understand the Requirement → Perform the Configuration/Activity → Execute the Process → Validate the Expected Outcome

The system then validates whether the required outcome has been achieved.

This makes the exam feel much closer to a real implementation scenario. Instead of simply asking, "Which option is correct?", the assessment is more focused on "Can you actually make this work in the system?"

How does this change the preparation approach?
Because of this change, I would not recommend preparing only by reading theory or memorising questions.

The SAP Learning Journey available through SAP Learning Hub is a very good starting point. It provides structured learning across the important areas of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition Sales and helps build the conceptual foundation required for the certification.

But while going through the Learning Journey, I would strongly recommend spending time in an SAP system as well.

For example, when learning about pricing, don't stop after understanding pricing procedures and condition types. Try creating the relevant configuration, maintain the required master data, create a sales order and check how the pricing is determined. If the expected condition does not appear, try to understand why.

The same approach can be followed for sales documents, delivery, billing, availability checking and other areas.

This hands-on practice makes a big difference because SAP Sales is highly interconnected. A small configuration or master-data setting in one area can affect the outcome somewhere else.

Focus on understanding the process
One of the important things I realised during preparation was that understanding the relationship between different configuration areas is more useful than memorising individual steps.

For example, when working with a sales order, it is important to understand how the sales document type, item category, schedule line category, pricing, partner determination and availability checking work together.

Similarly, understanding the complete flow from:

Sales Order → Delivery → Post Goods Issue → Billing

helps you identify where a particular issue may be coming from.

The same applies to areas such as credit management, account determination, output determination, text determination and partner determination.

You don't necessarily need to memorise every configuration screen. You should be comfortable enough with the concepts to understand what needs to be configured, where it needs to be configured, and what impact it will have on the business process.

My preparation approach
For my preparation, the combination that worked best was:

SAP Learning Journey + Conceptual Understanding + Hands-on Practice

I used the Learning Journey to understand the concepts and then tried to connect those concepts with actual system activities.

I found it particularly useful to practise a topic immediately after learning it instead of leaving all the hands-on practice until the end.

Also, don't be afraid of troubleshooting during practice. If a configuration does not produce the expected result, try to find the reason instead of immediately checking the solution.

That troubleshooting experience is valuable because, in a real SAP implementation, things rarely work perfectly on the first attempt.

entry.title: Taking the Leap: How Azra Turned a Distant Goal into a New Beginning
entry.content:
When Azra Gazibegovic first entered the SAP world almost ten years ago, SAP Certification felt like a “far, far-away dream.” 

She was a third-year Computer Science student when she joined DCCS IT Business Solutions as an intern and was assigned to its growing SAP team. Almost everything felt unfamiliar. She was learning ABAP while trying to make sense of SAP transactions, new tools, and concepts she had never encountered at university. 

At one point, Azra was offered the opportunity to move to a Java team, where she already had experience from her studies. It would have meant returning to more familiar territory. 

She decided to stay. 

“Today, I am very happy that I did.” 

After several years of hands-on experience with SAP, Azra decided to pursue her first certification. By then, she knew ABAP well and had built years of practical experience, but cloud technology was relatively new to her. With her company preparing to rebuild its product using cloud technology, the timing felt right to find out how strong her foundations really were — and push herself into something new. 

She didn’t do it alone. She found a study partner. 

“When I get motivated and excited about something, I tend to involve other people in it as well,” Azra says. She asked a colleague whether she wanted to pursue the certification with her. They prepared together for around two months, sat the exam on the same day, and both passed. 

For Azra, the result represented far more than passing an exam. 

“I proved to myself that I already had a strong foundation, and that something that had once seemed like a dream had now become a reality.” 

The experience did not formally change her job title. Instead, its impact showed up in less obvious ways. She became more confident exploring new areas of SAP and more proactive about keeping her knowledge current. 

Through her own preparation, Azra had learned how to navigate learning resources and find the information she needed to solve  a particular problem. As a mentor, she began  helping  colleagues learn how to find the information they needed, rather than simply giving them the answers. 

Today, Azra is a Senior SAP Developer and holds three SAP Certifications: Back-End Developer – ABAP Cloud, SAP Fiori Application Developer, and SAP Certified Associate – Design Thinking. She sees each one less as another credential to add to a list and more as a marker of where her interests and career were heading at the time. 

Design Thinking, for example, reflected a growing curiosity beyond purely technical development. As her role expanded to include mentoring, problem-solving and solution design, she began thinking about what a future closer to solution-oriented roles might look like. 

“For me, certification has become less about collecting credentials and more about choosing a direction I want to explore next.” 

The way Azra learns has changed too. When she entered the SAP ecosystem, she remembers large SAP books, blogs, experimenting in systems, project experience and, importantly, asking more experienced colleagues for help. Structured learning made knowledge easier to navigate. Now AI is changing that process again by making possible answers available almost instantly. 

But Azra believes that understanding the fundamentals is even more important. 

“The challenge is increasingly moving from finding a solution to understanding and validating the solution AI gives us.” 

It is a fitting perspective as SAP Certification marks its 30th anniversary. Technology has changed. The way people learn has changed. But for Azra, being part of this milestone comes back to something decidedly human: people helping other people learn. 

Throughout her own journey, colleagues shared their experience and encouraged her when she needed it. Sometimes the message was as simple as: “You can do it.” 

“It felt like someone had given me wings,” she says. “And almost instantly, I felt inspired to do the same for someone else.” 

For Azra, being part of 30 years of SAP Certification means continuing that cycle. Knowledge is learned, tested, shared, and eventually passed on to someone else. 

“I hope that, in my own small way, I can continue the same cycle, taking what others have given me and passing it on to someone else.” 

And for someone looking at their first certification today and wondering, as Azra once did, whether they are ready, her advice starts with those same four words: 

“YOU CAN DO IT.

There will never be a day when you can honestly say: ‘Now I know it all and I am 100% ready’. And that is okay. You don’t need to know everything before taking the next step,” she said and continued: “Challenge yourself. Let the learning happen along the way”.  

Ready to take your next step? Explore SAP Learning and see where your learning journey takes you.

entry.title: Score Report for System-Based Certification Exams Is Here
entry.content:
Earlier this year, we completed the transformation to performance-based certification at SAP, changing how we validate skills to better reflect how work gets done in the real world.

The response has been overwhelmingly positive. One important piece of the experience was still missing, though: a score report that gives you more insight into your exam performance.

That changes now.

We are proud to introduce score reports for system-based certification exams, providing a clear, topic-level view of your exam performance and helping you understand where you demonstrate proficiency and where to focus your learning next.

After completing a system-based certification exam, your score report provides a breakdown of your performance across the topics covered in the exam handbook you used during your assessment.

For each topic, you see:

  • The topic assessed
  • Your performance level
  • Your overall exam result

That gives you more transparency into your certification result and actionable insights to guide your next step

1.1. Score Report

Where to find your score report

Your Score Report is available for download in the “My Learning” area of learning.sap.com:

My Learning → Certification → ‘Certification you want to check’ → Score Report

1.2. My Learning

1.3. Score Report Download

⚠️Score Reports are available for all exams taken on or after October 9, 2026. Exams completed before this date will not have a score report generated.

How to read your score report

Your report includes exam details, your overall exam score, and your performance across individual exam topics. Each exam topic can have one of three performance labels:

  • Needs improvement: This topic is an area to strengthen. Your topic score was below the cut score.
  • Proficient: You met the expected standard. Your topic score reached the cut score.
  • Advanced: You clearly exceeded the expected standard. Your topic score was well above the cut score.

Some tasks you performed cover more than one topic. Use these labels as guidance on where to focus your learning.

Why score reports matter

Certification is about more than a pass-or-fail result. Understanding your performance can help you make your next learning decision with greater confidence.

If you didn’t pass your exam, your score report can help you identify the topics where you may want to strengthen your skills before trying again.

If you pass, your score report provides additional insight into where you demonstrated strengths and where you can continue to develop your expertise.

Your result tells you where you landed. Your score report helps you understand the journey.

entry.title: “Just Take the Exam”: Tammy Powlas’ Journey Through 25 Years of SAP Certification
entry.content:
When Tammy Powlas wanted to attend her first SAP Certification Academy, her boss had a different suggestion: take the exam first. 

It was 2000. Tammy had recently moved into consulting after working on a successful SAP go-live at a large telecommunications company. She had heard good things about the SAP Certification Academy and wanted to attend the Financial Accounting (FI) Academy. 

Instead, her boss encouraged her to go straight for the exam. 

“I think my first boss knew I could pass the exam without attending the Academy,” Tammy recalls. 

He was right. 

Tammy prepared independently by using SAP Help for the FI module. At the time, those learning materials came on CDs. She worked through the material while drawing on what she had already learned through experience. 

Looking back, passing those early Financial Accounting and Controlling exams remains one of the moments she is proudest of. 

“I am proud I took the FI-CO exams by just looking at the SAP Help.” 

That first exam became the beginning of a learning journey that would continue alongside Tammy’s career for the next 25 years. 

Today, learners have more ways to prepare and build their confidence. They can prepare for SAP Certification through free self-paced resources on SAP Learning, with additional guided learning and expert support through SAP Learning Hub.  

When Tammy moved into consulting, certification was valued in the profession. Later, after leaving consulting and moving into a different position, Strategic Enterprise Management became relevant to her work. This time, she attended the SAP Academy in Atlanta. 

Her memory of the experience is succinct: “It was intense.” 

As Tammy’s responsibilities expanded to include SAP Business Warehouse (BW), her learning evolved with them. Earning her BW certification had a particularly important effect. 

“Getting SAP Certified in BW made me confident in my job.” 

That confidence has remained one of the most meaningful parts of certification for Tammy. She never saw it primarily as a way to secure another position. Instead, certification gave her a reason to go deeper into a subject and understand it in a way her everyday work might not otherwise require. 

“Certification forces you to learn the material in a way you haven’t had to before,” she says. 

For Tammy, the result is simple: “It gives me confidence in the areas that I am certified in.” 

As Tammy’s career evolved, so did the areas in which she chose to certify, spanning FI, CO, BW, Strategic Enterprise Management and Accelerated SAP methodology. Each reflected a different area of her professional experience and learning. Some of that learning translated directly into her work. After becoming certified in the Accelerated SAP methodology, Tammy later worked as a project manager and followed the methodology closely throughout a project. The project was a success. 

Today, Tammy is a business analyst as well as an SAP Mentor and ASUG volunteer. She has also watched the experience of learning and becoming certified change considerably since that first exam in 2000. 

One of the biggest changes is practical. 

“Not having to fly to a location, for example, Boston or Atlanta, is a big change in certification,” Tammy says. Proctored exams have changed the experience too. 

Her journey offers a glimpse of just how much can change over the course of a career. Tammy began by studying SAP Help on CDs and travelling to SAP Academies. Twenty-five years later, professionals can access learning and certification in very different ways. 

But the part of her story that matters most has little to do with how the exam is delivered. 

It is about learning something more deeply. It is about challenging what you know. And sometimes, it is about discovering that you are more ready than you think. 

That idea has been there since Tammy’s first certification. Her boss believed she was ready to take the exam without attending the Academy first. Years later, after Tammy earned her most recent certification, the Associate-level SAP Business Warehouse (BW) certification, she received kudos from her boss’s boss. 

For someone considering their first SAP Certification today, Tammy recommends making use of the learning support now available. 

“I recommend joining the SAP Learning Hub, if possible,” she says, pointing to the value of learning with instructors and the certification guidance they can provide. 

Twenty-five years ago, Tammy thought the next step was attending an Academy. Someone else saw that she might already be ready for something bigger. 

So she took the exam. 

For anyone waiting until they feel completely ready to take their own next step, Tammy’s story offers another possibility: perhaps the learning you have already done has prepared you for more than you think. 

And if you are ready to find out what comes next, continue your learning journey with SAP Learning.
